messages:
Mia Chen: Quick design review — I tried the new 'toolbelt' flow in the playground. When I open a function def the schema preview is expanded by default and it pushes the call stack + inputs down. Feels heavy when I'm toggling between defs. Thoughts?

Samir Patel: Which part felt heavy — left rail (schema) or right pane (result)?

Mia Chen: Left rail mainly. The preview height is large and there's no compact summary. Example: I click fn -> page jumps, I lose my place in the run history. Screenshot: https://img.example/redwood/mock

Eli Torres: +1. Suggestion: show a 1-line summary row with name + type badges and an expand chevron. Expand should animate but not reflow the whole page. Also the label 'Schema (auto-detect)' is confusing.

Kate O'Neill: Copy suggestion: replace 'Schema (auto-detect)' with 'Schema preview — inferred'. Shorter, clearer.

Samir Patel: Accessibility note — keyboard focus currently lands on the expand chevron after opening; it should land on the first editable input instead. @DesignBot can we add an automated focus-order check?

DesignBot: Added a checklist comment on the PR: "focus order: open schema -> primary arg input receives focus". Also flagged keyboard shortcut consistency.

Mia Chen: Run history UX: tool-call entries show fn name + truncated args. Can we surface small param-type badges (string/number/file) so scanning is faster? Maybe 12–16px icons with alt text.

Eli Torres: Icons are fine, but watch contrast and motion. Use filled-outline tokens at 16px. We'll map param types to icons in the token library. Implementation will need a small rendering helper in the runlog component.

Kate O'Neill: Another nit — the button label varies across flows: sometimes it's 'Run' and other times 'Invoke'. We should pick one. My vote: 'Run' to match console.

Samir Patel: Agreed. We'll standardize on 'Run' and update copy system.

Mia Chen: For compact mode: collapse result previews by default and show a small 'Show result' link. Run history is noisy during quick dev loops.

Eli Torres: Dev/runtime note: collapsing results must keep KV cache intact so replay works — will coordinate with runtime team.

Kate O'Neill: I'll update the copy doc and push a small PR with the label changes + tooltip that says 'Press R to run'.

Mia Chen: Accessibility SR nit — screen readers currently read the expand control as just 'Expand'. Can we make it verbose: aria-label="Expand schema for function <name>" so context is preserved?

DesignBot: Filed issue #482 for screen-reader label improvements and added acceptance criteria. Assigned to @Eli Torres.

Samir Patel: Thanks all. I'll draft an interaction spec today with the compact summary row, param badges, and focus behavior. Will link a prototype — please comment inline once it's up.

Mia Chen: Sounds good. Quick UX poll: collapse-by-default or keep expanded-by-default?

Eli Torres: collapse-by-default for dev mode, expanded-by-default for first-time users. We can detect "first run" and override.

Kate O'Neill: Agree with Eli. Also adding a tiny hint: "Press ? for shortcuts" in the help menu.

Mia Chen: Perfect — thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Samir Patel: Leaving a short TODO list in the thread: 1) spec draft (Samir) 2) copy PR (Kate) 3) accessibility labels (Eli) 4) runtime KV check (Eli) 5) design review (Mia).

DesignBot: Noted. I added the TODO checklist to the PR description and linked this thread.
